A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-termini of fsTnTs are functionally distinct, and may play a role in the regulation of myofilament Ca2+ sensitivity.
fsTnT is a key regulator of thin-filament activation in fast skeletal muscle, and isoform-specific differences are due to changes in thin-filament regulation.
the isoform of fast skeletal troponins expressed by the muscle determines the myofilament Ca2+ sensitivity, which may be a key determinant of the contractile function of the muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal domain of fsTnTs containing the α-exon has a more favorable effect on the thin filament regulatory unit than that of the C-terminal domain with the β-exon.

fsTnT is not just a passive linker of the thin filament, but rather, it is involved in the regulation of myofilament Ca2+ sensitivity and may play a significant role in modulating contractile function.
fsTnT C-terminal sequence is a determinant of thin-filament activation.
